slot.brief: Find the domain of a composite/square-root rational function as an intersection of conditions.

verdicts.working: Factor the radicand as \((x-1)(x+1)/(x-2)\). It is nonnegative on \([-1,1]\) and \((2,\infty)\); exclude \(x=2\).

working:
$\displaystyle \frac{x^2-1}{x-2}=\frac{(x-1)(x+1)}{x-2}\geq0,\quad x\neq2$
Critical points: $-1,1,2$.
Sign is nonnegative on $[-1,1]$ and $(2,\infty)$. Independent check: Factor the radicand as \((x-1)(x+1)/(x-2)\). It is nonnegative on \([-1,1]\) and \((2,\infty)\); exclude \(x=2\).
solution:
For the square root to be defined, the radicand must satisfy $\dfrac{(x-1)(x+1)}{x-2}\geq 0$, with $x\neq 2$.
The critical points are $-1,1,2$; the expression is nonnegative on $[-1,1]$ and $(2,\infty)$.
Hence the domain is $[-1,1]\cup(2,\infty)$.
